To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interference effects between the Z′- and the Z-boson can be substantial, but can be reduced to the level of $ \mathcal {O}$(10%) by a quasi-model-independent cut on the invariant mass of the dilepton system.

interference effects between a Z′-bosonsignal and the Standard Model backgrounds are important, and can be reduced to $ \sim $ 10% level by a quasi-model-independent invariant mass window cut, valid over a large range in Z′-bosomass.

the Z′- boson interference with the Standard Model background is a model dependent effect that can be substantial, and that it can be controlled to $ \mathO $ (10%) by using a model independent cut on the invariant mass, which is approximately constant for a wide range and does not scale with Z′-mass.
In summary, our research is concerned with

two main aspects of the Z′ search at the LHC:     1. the interference effects of the Z′ signal in Drell-Ya, which can be substantial;     2. a “magic cut” that reduces the model-dependent Z′-bosons interference to a few percent.
the following questions: (a) What are the interference effects between an additional neutral spin-1 boson and the Standard Mode background at the LHC?
the interference between the Standard Model background and an extra neutral spin one boson, Z′, in the Drell–Yan channel at the Large Hadron Collider.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
interference effects are not a problem for Z′ searches in the Drell–Yan channel at the 8 TeV LHC, provided that the invariant mass window cut is applied.

the interference effects in Z′-bosons searches are important and should be taken into account, but the quasi-model-independent invariant mass window cut provides an effective way to reduce the model-dependence of the interference effects, and therefore, the experimental collaborations could use the suggested invariant mass cut in the Z′- searches.

the interference contribution is model-dependent and should be taken into account in a model-specific way, but that a quasi-model-independent analysis, with the invariant mass cut suggested, is possible, and that it may lead to a more sensitive search for Z′-bosons at the LHC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
one can perform a quasi-model-independent analysis for the Z′ search, while the interference effects can be reduced to a level of $ \mathcal {O}$(10%).
the Z′ interference effects are not negligible and should be taken into account in the analyses.
the Z′ interference effects are not a nuisance, but can be controlled and used for the discovery of new physics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current experimental searches and interpretations of the Z′ searches at the LHC should be revisited in light of the interference effects.
the Z′-search results should be presented with an indication of the interference contribution to the signal, which should be included in the systematic error.
the current experimental analyses for Z′-bosons are not model-independent.
